cohort: The study included women who had a subsequent pregnancy following OASIS and women without a history of such injuries, all of whom delivered in a tertiary medical center between 2015 and 2019.
finding: There was no significant difference in the mean interpregnancy interval between women with and without prior OASIS, but women with prior OASIS were significantly more likely to experience a repeat perineal tear, an episiotomy, or a cesarean section in their subsequent delivery.
mod_finding: Women who experienced OASIS were significantly more likely to have an elective or emergency cesarean section in their subsequent delivery.
